A later Friday WSJ Treasury report gave 10Y 5.133% and 2Y 4.850%, implying +28.3bp (not a synchronized closing pair). No new Open Watch events; no new cash-session evidence or material change from prior bearish elevated-downside assessment.

editorial.marketOverview: Friday ended with Nasdaq Composite down 0.91%, S&P 500 down 0.42% and Dow up 0.09%, while Nasdaq nevertheless rose 2.3% over the week. Nvidia's $162.85 close, down 2.01%, highlights persistent AI leadership pressure. Earlier SOX losses were intraday and must not be misrepresented as official closing returns. The weekend has supplied no new cash-session confirmation.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the previous 17:10 EST assessment, AP confirms the Nasdaq's 2.3% weekly gain and Yahoo Finance confirms Nvidia's $162.85 Friday close. A Friday WSJ report provides a newer 10Y/2Y pair of 5.133% and 4.850%, yielding a correctly scaled +28.3bp spread, although the quote times are not verified synchronized closing marks. Open Watch remains unchanged at 163 events. These refinements do not establish a material change to the three-session path.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Technology's Friday underperformance and Nvidia-specific uncertainty support an elevated downside skew, offset by the week's broader gains and a slightly softer monthly producer-price print. High yields and a hawkish Fed outlook continue to pressure long-duration growth valuations. The +28.3bp spread is a reported-Friday derived figure, not an official curve settlement. Without fresh synchronized SOX, breadth and volatility, neither capitulation nor stabilization is proven.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 16 tests whether Friday's technology weakness attracts buyers or extends into broader Nasdaq selling. Tuesday November 17 brings reported retail-sales and major earnings risk, culminating in Nvidia's expected after-close report. Wednesday November 18 is the key session for the actual market response to Nvidia results and guidance. Bearish elevated downside remains the base case, with an oversold rebound plausible but unconfirmed; no precise odds or price targets are warranted.
editorial.bullCase: A Monday recovery holding Friday lows and accompanied by positive breadth, SOX outperformance, lower volatility and easing yields would challenge the bearish interpretation. The Nasdaq's 2.3% weekly advance and softer monthly PPI show that demand has not disappeared. A favorable Nvidia report could improve AI-sector sentiment, but no response can be assumed before release.
editorial.bearCase: Failure to hold Friday lows, renewed semiconductor underperformance and deteriorating breadth would confirm further downside pressure. Elevated yields and concerns about AI leadership or financing could magnify a negative Nvidia earnings surprise and spill into Wednesday. A high-volatility gap remains a scenario rather than an observed event.
editorial.watchNext: Verify official QQQ/SOX closes and synchronized Monday prices, VXN/VIX, Nasdaq breadth, Friday oil settlements and live matched 10Y/2Y yields; review direct CME FedWatch when accessible. Confirm Nvidia earnings timing via issuer and monitor Tuesday retail-sales data and Wednesday earnings reaction. Recheck curated Open Watch events for genuinely new developments.
